clue.text: From riverside, leave for a day off

parts.note: a riverside is a bank, the land along a river's edge
leave from work is a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone takes a day off and heads away from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: BANK HOLIDAY is a British public holiday, when banks and most offices close.
explanation.definitionFit: A public holiday is a day when people are excused from work.

clue.text: The script is dotty, I feel

definitions.text: The script is dotty, I feel

parts.words: The script is dotty, I feel
parts.note: a writing system made of raised dots that is read with the fingertips

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the writing they are reading is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' means crazy on the surface but literally made of dots, and 'I feel' is how it is read, by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The tactile writing system for blind readers is formed of raised dots.

indicators.note: a horrible thing is a ghastly mess, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fear of the dark as something dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours when the sun is down are dark.

parts.note: the greeting of clasping palms, read as a trembling of the palm in fear

explanation.surface: A greeting that gives away someone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting split in two describes a palm trembling, the sign of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and pumping palms is a common greeting, and a trembling palm shows nerves.

clue.text: After a city, island on river seems a beastly place

indicators.note: after puts the following letters behind the city in the answer
in a down clue on means placed above, so the island sits over the river

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, an American city
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island city beside a river seems a horrible place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is its home, literally a place for beasts.

parts.note: dead means completely, as in dead right
beat means worn out

explanation.surface: A tramp is completely worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle, penniless loafer is a down-and-out.

indicators.note: about means the story wraps around the letter for the East

parts.note: a yarn is a long tale
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale about the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave it, the verb sense.

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone turns a kitchen gadget around.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean spins or revolves.

indicators.note: falsely says the letters are presented wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat's move that won over the English through deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges CHARMED into DEMARCH, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A demarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation.

indicators.note: something in revolution is turned over and overthrown, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: In a nation in upheaval, rents are being charged again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges the letters of RENT AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation.

clue.text: Antiquity, with scripture, is a factor

parts.note: antiquity is great age
NT is the New Testament, Christian scripture

explanation.surface: Ancient times and holy writ are said to be an influence.
explanation.walkthrough: A factor in the older sense is someone who acts on another's behalf, a steward or business representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a representative who manages business for someone else, a synonym.

clue.text: The French exam is very up-to date

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of the
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A French test is described as thoroughly modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand new is the most recent of its kind.

clue.text: A cake, desired at first by worker, is plentiful

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word desired

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer longs for a cake, and there is plenty to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a supply that is ample, more than enough.

clue.text: Make more popular, giving complete attention

parts.note: to complete something is to end it
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Paying full attention to people wins favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To win affection for someone is to make them better liked.

clue.text: Representative from Georgia coming in to cancel

indicators.note: coming in means the state's letters enter the word for cancel

parts.note: to cancel text is to delete it
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A delegate from Georgia arrives to call something off.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to act for others, a synonym.

definitions.meaning: to barrack is to jeer or heckle a speaker or team
the buildings where troops are housed

explanation.surface: Protesters picket an army base.
explanation.definitionFit: Heckling a speaker is one sense; the other is the military buildings that house troops.

parts.note: read not as a rigged court case but as a try-out of a stage show

explanation.surface: A political trial staged for propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: A show trial is a sham court case; here it means a trial run of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance before opening night is a test of the production.

clue.text: Hard currency all accepted, a sign of sterling value

indicators.note: accepted means the outer letters take in the word all

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: Strong money accepted everywhere signals real worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp on silver or gold certifies its purity, so it marks genuine quality.

parts.note: a dead-end street, named with a phrase borrowed from French, literally the bottom of the bag

explanation.surface: A dead-end street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The term for a dead-end road is French in origin, hence 'Parisian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street closed at one end is a dead end, and English uses the French phrase for it.

clue.text: Splendid chap in bed has cigar

indicators.note: in places the splendid chap inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a hero is an admirable man

explanation.surface: A fine fellow smokes in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar cut square at both ends.

definitions.meaning: the word said when raising glasses to drink a health
something that gladdens the heart, as good news does

explanation.surface: A drink raised to someone, and a comforting thought.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the call made when drinking to someone, and also a verb meaning gladdens or comforts.

clue.text: Odds on fish having a little glittering plate

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the odds above the fishing word

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at the start of a race
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: Betting on a fishing trip that brings a shiny dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small shiny piece of metal sewn on clothes, a sequin.

definitions.meaning: a very thin, delicate kind of china
a hatching chick cracks its way out of its casing

explanation.surface: A chick smashes a piece of fine china.
explanation.definitionFit: Very thin translucent china takes its name from the shell a hatching chick breaks through.

clue.text: In Marrakesh, a remarkable collection of women

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A notable gathering of women in a Moroccan city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the answer within 'MarrakesH A REMarkable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a household, or the wives and concubines living there.

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the headgear of a university graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat.

indicators.note: almost means the word all loses its last letter

parts.note: ice is coldness or stiff formality of manner

explanation.surface: A young woman is described as stiffly formal.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in the heroine of Wonderland.

definitions.meaning: the soft wormlike young of an insect

explanation.surface: Something to eat for an insect's young.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for food and also an insect's young.

indicators.note: visible says the answer can be seen within the words not terribly

explanation.surface: An animal in the water is hard to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visible' shows the answer within 'nOT TERribly', which the surface says is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful mammal that lives along rivers.

definitions.meaning: what police do on detaining a suspect

explanation.surface: Police detain someone for hitting another.
explanation.definitionFit: It is what police do when detaining someone, and also means eye-catching.

clue.text: Compel to give credence to fantasy

parts.note: to make someone do something is to compel them
to give credence to something is to believe it

explanation.surface: Forcing people to accept a story that is pure invention.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending, or a world of pretence, is fantasy.
